cues.en: Now that we know what heat pumps are and how they work, it's time to talk a little more about their future. If you've not seen the first video, well you definitely should fix that before watching this one, as there will be a lot of stuff we talk about here that assumes prior knowledge. I'll summon a card. Bippity boppity card! Great! A link is below and probably in a pinned comment too. You ever heard about those? They're neat. I want to start with a clarification of sorts.
cues.zh: 既然我们已经知道热泵是什么以及它是如何工作的，就该来聊聊它的未来了。如果你还没看过第一期视频，强烈建议先去补一下再看这期，因为我们接下来要讲的很多内容都需要先验知识。我放个卡片出来，变！搞定！链接在下方，可能置顶评论里也有。你见过那种置顶吗？挺好玩的。在开始之前，我想先澄清几点。

cues.en: Heat pumps definitely are the future of home heating, at least if I can help it, but they're also not new. And some people hate them. It seems for every person who thinks heat pumps are wicked, neato, closest thing to free energy out there devices, that's me. There's another who hates theirs with a passion. Allow me to submit that you don't hate your heat pump, you hate your thermostat. See, as we learned, as the outdoor temperature approaches freezing, it gets harder for air source heat pumps to work.
cues.zh: 热泵绝对是家庭供暖的未来——至少在我看来是这样——但它其实也不算什么新鲜事物了。而且有些人甚至很讨厌它。似乎每有一个人觉得热泵是不可思议、超酷、最接近免费能源的神器——没错，那就是我——就会有另一个人打心底里讨厌它。容我斗胆说一句：你讨厌的不是热泵，而是你的温控器。你看，正如我们学过的那样，当室外温度逼近冰点时，空气源热泵的工作难度就会增加。

cues.en: A smaller temperature difference between the source of heat and the evaporator absorbing it causes the efficiency of heat pumps to drop and eventually their output as well. Unfortunately, it is under these precise conditions that the demand for heat goes up. It's kind of a bummer. So most systems with heat pumps have some sort of backup heat source, be it electric resistive heat, often this is called the heat strips, though I prefer to think of it as a giant hair dryer, or a fuel-fired furnace might be utilized.
cues.zh: 热源与吸收热量的蒸发器之间的温差变小，会导致热泵的效率下降，最终其制热输出也会随之降低。遗憾的是，恰恰就是在这种极端条件下，供暖需求才会激增。这确实有点让人扫兴。所以大多数带有热泵的系统都会配有某种备用热源，比如电阻加热——通常被称为电热条，不过我更喜欢把它想象成一个巨型吹风机——或者使用燃油/燃气炉。

cues.en: The trouble is, until quite recently the thermostats controlling these systems would just run the heat pump as hard as it could until the output wasn't enough to maintain the set point. Only then would they switch to the auxiliary heat. That meant that air coming out of your heat vents would get milder to the point it was barely heat at all before the thermostat gave up and switched heat sources. That is undoubtedly annoying, and if you've lived with a heating system that behaves like this I can see why you wouldn't like it.
cues.zh: 问题在于，直到不久前，控制这些系统的温控器还只会死命运行热泵，直到它的输出完全无法维持设定温度为止。只有到了那个时候，它才会切换到辅助供暖。这意味着，从出风口吹出来的空气会越来越温吞，甚至几乎感觉不到热气，直到温控器彻底放弃并切换热源。这毫无疑问很烦人，如果你的供暖系统也是这副德行，我完全理解你为什么会讨厌它。

cues.en: But it doesn't have to be that way, and it's not the fault of the heat pump. Instead of trying to run the heat pump until it just isn't enough anymore, a more thoughtful thermostat could handle things more thoughtfully. If the heating system can determine its current coefficient of performance, it can determine whether it makes sense to run the heat pump in the first place. You could even program at which COP it should switch to auxiliary heat. That would allow you to prioritize comfort, energy costs, or emissions.
cues.zh: 但其实大可不必这样，而且这也不是热泵本身的错。与其死脑筋地一直运行热泵直到它彻底撑不住，一个更智能的温控器完全可以把事情处理得更体贴。如果供暖系统能算出它当前的性能系数，就能直接判断从一开始开热泵是否划算。你甚至可以设定在哪个 COP 值下切换到辅助供暖。这样你就能自由权衡，优先考虑舒适度、能源成本还是碳排放了。

cues.en: Now, if your backup heat is electric, any COP greater than one will benefit you from a cost and emissions perspective, and that's largely why these systems will use the heat pump as long as they possibly can. It's saving you money, you ungr- But you can still use this to force the backup heat on before you notice the output falling if that's what you really wanted. If you have natural gas or some other fuel as your backup heat, you could choose to input the COP that is your break-even point on cost.
cues.zh: 现在，如果你的备用热是电，任何大于 1 的 COP 从成本和排放角度看都对你有利，这也是这些系统会尽可能长时间使用热泵的主要原因。它在帮你省钱，你这不知好歹的——但如果你真想这样，仍可以在察觉到输出下降前强制开启备用热。如果备用热是天然气或其他燃料，你可以输入成本盈亏平衡点对应的 COP。

cues.en: Now here in the Chicago area we have pretty cheap electricity and pretty cheap gas. By my calculations you need a COP of about four in order for a heat pump to beat the cost of gas here. That's certainly achievable on many winter days with a heat pump and certainly in the fall and early spring, but many times it isn't and if you had a thermostat which was aware of the current COP and could switch to auxiliary heat based on it,
cues.zh: 在芝加哥地区，我们的电和天然气都挺便宜。按我的计算，热泵要在这里比燃气更省钱，COP 需要达到约 4。用热泵在很多冬季日子肯定能达到，在秋季和早春当然也行，但很多时候达不到；如果你的恒温器知道当前 COP，并能据此切换到辅助热，

cues.en: Well, you'd be able to optimize for heating cost. Just compare your costs of energy sources, figure out what the COP break even point is, and set your system up accordingly. This is actually a legitimate use for smart thermostats. Even if the heating system can't determine its own COP, which many simpler systems can't, that can be reasonably predicted based upon outdoor temperatures and system specs.
cues.zh: 那你就能针对供暖成本做优化。只要比较各能源的成本，算出 COP 盈亏平衡点，再相应设置系统。这其实是智能恒温器的一个正当用途。即使供暖系统无法确定自身 COP（很多简单系统做不到），也可以根据室外温度和系统规格合理预测。

cues.en: A thermostat that can determine outdoor conditions can use this to its advantage, and knowing the outdoor humidity can even help it determine how often it needs to defrost the outside unit. Of course, this can be done locally with a temperature and humidity sensor, but if your thermostat were aware of the current energy mix on the grid in your area, it could also help reduce emissions by bending the COP changeover depending on what's advantageous.
cues.zh: 能判断室外条件的恒温器可以利用这一点，知道室外湿度甚至能帮它确定室外机多久需要除霜一次。当然，这可以用温湿度传感器在本地完成，但如果你的恒温器知道当地电网当前的能源结构，它还能根据什么更有利来调整 COP 切换点，从而帮助减排。

cues.en: Ideally, we'd have some sort of pricing structure where the cost of each energy source was related to its emissions, but that's getting deeper than this video needs to go. Oh, and speaking of defrosts, if you have a simpler heat pump system you might be very aware of when that happens because the outdoor unit makes a tremendous racket. If that's a reason you don't like heat pumps, you should know that this is also not a necessary thing by any means. A lot of domestic HVAC stuff is controlled with
cues.zh: 理想情况下，我们应该有某种定价结构，让每种能源的成本与其排放挂钩，但这超出了本视频要深入的范围。哦，说到除霜，如果你用的是更简单的热泵系统，你可能很清楚除霜何时发生，因为室外机会发出巨大噪音。如果这是你不喜欢热泵的原因，那你应该知道这绝不是必然的。很多家用暖通空调设备只靠

cues.en: little to no brains, if you will. Often the thermostat is literally the only thing in control of the outside unit, and simpler systems will just slam the reversing valve while the compressor is still running. And that's what's causing that racket. If instead the compressor were stopped before it reversed, allowing pressures to equalize, it would be much less noticeable. That's how this minisplit heat pump does it, and to my mind that's obviously better.
cues.zh: 几乎为零的智能来控制，可以这么说。通常恒温器实际上就是唯一控制室外机的东西，而更简单的系统会在压缩机仍在运行时直接猛切四通阀。这就是噪音的来源。如果反过来，在换向之前先停压缩机，让压力平衡，就会不明显得多。这台迷你分体式热泵就是这么做的，在我看来显然更好。

cues.en: I also can't see how changing the direction while the compressor runs isn't somewhat rough on it, but apparently it's not so bad because lots of systems do this very thing. Anyway, the point here is the little annoyances you may have with your heat pump system are probably nothing to do with it being a heat pump. Instead, it's simply bad design, or a case of misaligned priorities.
cues.zh: 我也想不通在压缩机运转时换向怎么会不伤机器，但显然问题不大，因为很多系统就是这么干的。总之，这里的关键在于，你对热泵系统的那些小抱怨，很可能根本不是热泵本身的问题。相反，这纯粹是糟糕的设计，或者是产品侧重点没摆对。

cues.en: In my opinion, air conditioning systems like the one I just installed that have no reversing capabilities should not exist. There is no reason this device cannot provide low emissions heating other than a few components are missing from it which made it slightly cheaper to build. This is a case of but sometimes thinking leading to the embrace of less flexible systems for virtually no reason and it's dumb.
cues.zh: 在我看来，像我刚装的这种不能反向制热的空调系统，根本就不该存在。这台设备完全有能力提供低碳供暖，唯一的阻碍只是省掉了几个零件让造价稍微便宜了点。这就是那种“因噎废食”的思维，毫无道理地倒向了灵活性更差的系统，简直蠢透了。

cues.en: Yes, in my climate there are many days in the winter where an air source heat pump would leave me in the cold. And that's a terrifying prospect. I completely get it. Nearly everyone around me has natural gas or occasionally propane heating because in the deepest depths of the winter you frankly need it. But since nearly everyone around me also has central air conditioning for our sweltering hot summers,
cues.zh: 没错，在我这种气候环境下，冬天确实有很多天，单靠空气源热泵会把你冻个半死。这种前景确实挺吓人的，我完全理解。我周围几乎所有人都在用天然气，或者偶尔用丙烷供暖，因为到了数九寒冬，你坦白讲真的离不开它。但既然我周围几乎所有人都为了熬过酷暑装了中央空调，

cues.en: They already have a heat pump, but it can only go one way because as of now, few people see the point of redundant heating systems when you have cheap natural gas anyway. But since whenever the COP of a heat pump exceeds 2.5, we can heat our homes with less fuel burned and ultimately lower emissions, why would we not want to make the air conditioner reversible for the many days of the year when that's absolutely possible? Well, frankly, the biggest barrier right now is direct cost to the consumer.
cues.zh: 那他们手里其实就已经有一台热泵了，只是它只能单向运行；因为就目前而言，既然都有便宜的天然气了，几乎没人觉得有必要搞一套备用供暖系统。但只要热泵的 COP 超过 2.5，我们就能少烧燃料给家里供暖，最终降低排放，那为什么不在一年中完全能做到的那些天里，把空调做成可逆的呢？坦白讲，眼下最大的障碍就是消费者的直接成本。

cues.en: As I said, in my area, unless you can get to a COP of 4, it's just not cost effective to run a heat pump over burning natural gas. And since there are many, many days in the winter where that COP is a lofty goal, even if running the heat pump is more climate friendly, it may not be more wallet friendly. The added cost of a heat pump may never make financial sense in my area, no matter how small that added cost might be.
cues.zh: 正如我所说，在我们这儿，除非 COP 能达到 4，否则开热泵就是不如烧天然气划算。而冬天的很多日子里，这个 COP 都是个可望不可即的目标，所以即使开热泵更环保，钱包也未必吃得消。在我们这儿，多花在热泵上的成本可能永远也回不了本，不管这点差价有多微不足道。

cues.en: At least, so long as externalities remain free to energy providers. Hope! Too deep alert! And that is why they're not standard equipment around here. Yet. But it should be noted that the financial practicality of a heat pump will depend entirely on your cost of heating fuel. If it's not natural gas, or even if it is but it's more expensive for you, that math will be different. Now, if I were king, I'd proclaim that every central air conditioning system sold
cues.zh: 至少，只要能源供应商还不需要为外部环境成本买单，情况就会如此。打住！扯太深了！这就是为什么它们在这儿还没成为标配——至少目前还不是。但必须说明的是，热泵在经济上划不划算，完全取决于你的供暖燃料成本。如果用的不是天然气，或者虽然是天然气但价格更贵，那笔账算出来可就不一样了。要是由我说了算，我一定会宣布所有售出的中央空调系统

cues.en: must be reversible. It's equipment with a 10-20 year service life, and who knows what the availability and cost of heating fuel will be in 2041. Plus, we keep making strides in system efficiency, and air source heat pumps are becoming viable in colder and colder climates. In fact, I just read a piece on their use in Alaska. It can absolutely be done, even up there.
cues.zh: 都必须是可逆的。这类设备的寿命长达 10 到 20 年，谁知道 2041 年供暖燃料的供应和价格会变成什么样。更何况，系统的能效还在不断突破，空气源热泵适用的气候环境也越来越冷。事实上，我刚读了一篇关于热泵在阿拉斯加应用的文章。就算在那儿，它也完全应付得来。

cues.en: But if you really want a heat pump to work in the coldest of the cold using the least amount of energy, you gotta go underground. Look down. See that? It's the ground. Turn around. There's a human scu- Sorry. Thinking of something else. You know how we have water pipes going every which way underground and even in the dead of winter they don't freeze? Usually. Well, that's because the Earth is warm.
cues.zh: 但如果你真想让热泵在最冷的地方用最少的能量工作，那就得往地下走。往下看。看到了吗？这就是地面。转过去。有个人体雕塑——抱歉，想岔了。你知道我们地下的水管四通八达，哪怕隆冬时节也不冻吗？通常如此。那是因为地球是暖的。

cues.en: Dig just a few feet below the surface and you'll find the frost line. Below this imaginary line, the ground doesn't freeze. Where that line is changes depending on where you are, but it's there! Management was just really bad about marking it when they built the place.
cues.zh: 往下挖几英尺，就会遇到冻结线。在这条假想线以下，地面不会冻结。这条线在哪因地点而异，但它确实存在！只是当年建造这地方时，管理层实在不擅长把它标出来。

cues.en: Since heat pumps are great at extracting and concentrating heat energy from relatively cool places, and since there's a place right below our feet that doesn't get cold enough to freeze water no matter how cold it is outside, if we could just get the heat energy from that place to the evaporator of a heat pump, we could get more than enough heat to warm our homes no matter what time of year it is. And wouldn't you know it? This is a thing we know how to do.
cues.zh: 热泵很擅长从相对凉的地方提取并集中热能；而我们脚下正好有个地方，不管外面多冷，都不会冷到把水冻住。只要能把那里的热能送到热泵的蒸发器，不管什么季节，我们都能得到足够多的热量来给家里供暖。你猜怎么着？这事我们早就会做了。

cues.en: Ground source, or geothermal heat pumps, scavenge heat from the ground below the frost line. There are two main ways to do this, and both involve using an intermediary fluid to transfer heat energy. And yes, some newer ideas don't use an intermediary fluid, but we're not talking about them today. Instead of an outside unit like this with a large fan-driven refrigerant-to-air heat exchanger, these systems will have a refrigerant-to-liquid heat exchanger.
cues.zh: 地源热泵，也叫地热热泵，从冻结线以下的地层中汲取热量。主要有两种做法，都需要用中间流体来传递热能。没错，一些新思路不用中间流体，但今天不讲那些。它们不再像这样在室外装一个带大风扇、靠制冷剂到空气换热的室外机，而是配一个制冷剂到液体的换热器。

cues.en: There's no law saying evaporators have to look like this, after all. Inside your home, the equipment doesn't look too much different from a normal furnace or air handler, but the compressor, and sometimes there's more than one, as well as both heat exchangers are all right here. And to those worried about noise from the compressors, don't worry, there's plenty of sound deadening. Engineers are smart. What's special about these systems is where they're getting their heat from.
cues.zh: 毕竟，没有哪条法律规定蒸发器必须长这样。在你家里，设备看起来和普通炉子或空气处理机差别不大，但压缩机——有时还不止一台——以及两个换热器，全都在这里。担心压缩机噪音的人不用怕，隔音措施很到位。工程师很聪明。这些系统的特别之处，在于它们从哪里取热。

cues.en: A long, closed loop of piping filled with a mixture of water and antifreeze is pumped in a circuit out of the home and underground, where the liquid will absorb heat from the earth before being brought back inside. This now-warmed liquid is fed to the heat exchanger, which will absorb and concentrate that heat with the help of our friend, the refrigeration cycle. The refrigerant is then squeezed into the condenser and that heat is released into the air and ultimately the living space.
cues.zh: 一条长长的闭合管道环路，里面灌满水和防冻液的混合液，被泵送着从家里流向地下，液体在那里吸收大地的热量，然后再被送回室内。现在变暖的液体被送入换热器，换热器借助我们的老朋友——制冷循环——吸收并集中这份热量。接着制冷剂被压入冷凝器，热量释放到空气中，最终进入居住空间。

cues.en: The benefit of doing this is that no matter what the air temperature is outside, the temperature of the fluid returning from the ground loop will be a near constant 50 degrees Fahrenheit or about 10 Celsius. That temperature allows a heat pump to run at peak performance and efficiency, delivering a nearly constant, near maximum COP at full output, no matter what. Right now, you can expect it to always meet or exceed a COP of 4, and that will undoubtedly improve as technology advances.
cues.zh: 这样做的好处在于，无论室外气温如何，从地埋管循环回路流回的液体温度都会几乎恒定在华氏50度（约合摄氏10度）左右。这个温度能让热泵以最高性能和效率运转，在全负荷输出时始终提供近乎恒定、接近极限的COP（能效比）。眼下，它的COP基本能稳定在4甚至更高，而且随着技术进步，这个数值毫无疑问还会提升。

cues.en: And that's obviously a huge deal. A home with a geothermal heat pump needs significantly less energy to heat than any other heating technology available today. Unless you count home design itself and want to bring up the passive house, but that's a topic for another time. Even with an entirely fossil fuel powered electrical infrastructure, emissions are drastically reduced when using a ground source heat pump.
cues.zh: 这显然是件了不起的大事。安装地源热泵的住宅在供暖方面的能耗，要远远低于当今市面上的任何其他供暖技术。除非你把房屋本身的设计也算进来，想聊聊被动房，不过那是另一个话题了。即使完全依靠化石燃料发电的基础设施供电，使用地源热泵也能大幅减少碳排放。

cues.en: Remember, exceed 2.5 and you're getting more energy out of burning natural gas in a power plant and sending its energy the zippy zappy way than natural gas itself contains. That's astonishing and yet completely possible. Also important is that methane, the main component of natural gas, is a potent greenhouse gas, and the infrastructure we use to transport it to homes across the country is notoriously leaky.
cues.zh: 记住，只要COP超过2.5，你在发电厂燃烧天然气并把电力噼里啪啦输送过来的能量产出，就已经超过了天然气本身所蕴含的能量。这听起来令人惊叹，但却完全可行。同样重要的是，天然气的主要成分甲烷是一种强效温室气体，而我们用来向全国各地家庭输送天然气的基础设施，泄漏问题那是出了名的严重。

cues.en: Not requiring that infrastructure in the first place provides its own emissions reduction. What's more, the much lower energy requirement of homes with geothermal heat pumps opens up many more opportunities, particularly when it comes to renewable and locally generated sources of power. Oh, and of course, these systems are entirely reversible. In the summer months,
cues.zh: 从源头上不再需要这些基础设施，本身就能带来减排效果。更重要的是，地源热泵住宅极低的能耗需求带来了更多可能性，特别是在可再生能源和本地发电方面。哦，当然，这些系统是完全可逆的。到了夏季，

cues.en: Well, below the frost line, the earth stays colder than the air outside. So in cooling mode, the system simply puts heat back into the earth. It's actually almost poetic. That heat ends up simply being borrowed in the winter months and returned in the summer. And being able to transfer it into a cool liquid means no matter how hot it gets outside, the system will run at peak performance. Neat. So what's the catch? Eleven words.
cues.zh: 在冻土层之下，大地的温度始终低于室外的空气。因此在制冷模式下，系统只需把热量送回地下。这其实挺有诗意的：热量只是在冬天被借了出来，到了夏天又物归原主。而且能把热量转移到低温液体中，意味着无论室外多热，系统都能以最高性能运行。真棒。那么，代价是什么呢？简单一句话：

cues.en: the upfront cost and disruptive nature of the ground loop installation. That second part's getting better, but unless you happen to be lucky and have access to some natural body of water like a pond that's deep and large enough to use as your heat source, which is another way to go about it by the way, there will have to be a network of piping installed under the ground to collect and transport its heat energy.
cues.zh: 前期成本高昂，且地埋管的安装施工破坏性很大。后一点现在正逐步改善，但除非你足够幸运，能用上某些又深又大的天然水体（比如池塘）作为热源——顺便说一句，这也是另一种可行的途径——否则就必须在地下铺设一套管道网络，来收集并输送地底的热能。

cues.en: For a long time, this meant excavating a large area around a home down to several feet, think about a meter-ish, below the frost line. Then you'd go all loopy with a bunch of piping and cover it back up. Hopefully you remembered to put the ends of that pipe somewhere useful. But that's really disruptive and requires a large area of lawn or similar open space. I mean, if you're building a new house somewhere and have room, please just do it. It's the perfect time.
cues.zh: 长期以来，这意味着要在房子周围挖一大片地，向下挖几英尺——大约一米左右——到冻土线以下。然后绕来绕去铺上一大堆管道，再回填。希望你没忘了把管道末端留在有用的地方。但这破坏性很大，还需要大片草坪或类似空地。我是说，如果你正好在某处建新房、又有空间，那就尽管做吧。这是最佳时机。

cues.en: Oh, and one interesting idea that's taking hold is community ground loops. A bunch of homes in a new development can be hooked up to a large, shared ground loop that's piped into each home. They each have their own heat pumps extracting energy from the fluid, but the geothermal equipment is shared, maximizing its potential and lowering the cost per user. But if you want to add a ground loop to an existing home site, it kinda sucks and sometimes isn't possible.
cues.zh: 哦，还有一个逐渐流行起来的有趣想法：社区共享地埋环路。新开发项目里的多栋住宅可以接入一个大型共享地埋环路，再分管道通到每户。每户有自己的热泵，从流体中提取能量，但地热设备是共享的，从而最大化利用潜力、降低每个用户的成本。不过，如果想给现有住宅加装地埋环路，那就挺糟心的，有时根本做不到。

cues.en: However, a more recent and exciting development is the use of vertical drilling to go deeper rather than broader. Using equipment similar to that which is used to dig a well for drinking water, a borehole can be dug hundreds of feet below the soil, and a rather simple bit of piping down and then back up can be run to extract that earthy warmth. This is much less disruptive and easier to accomplish in areas with denser housing and little green space.
cues.zh: 不过，更近也更令人兴奋的进展，是用垂直钻井往深处钻，而不是往宽处挖。使用类似打饮用水井的设备，可以往地下钻几百英尺，然后下入一套相当简单的管道，再返回上来，提取地下的热量。这种方式破坏小得多，在住房密集、绿地很少的地区也更容易实施。

cues.en: Dandelion Energy is one company installing such systems. Now, these aren't cheap. Their own website admits that this is going to cost about as much as a small car, and depending on how your energy is priced, you may never recoup that investment. But, regardless of where you are, it will reduce greenhouse emissions, and hopefully energy starts getting priced to reflect that. Oh sorry, going too deep again.
cues.zh: Dandelion Energy 就是一家安装这类系统的公司。不过这些系统不便宜。他们自己的网站也承认，费用大约相当于一辆小型汽车，而且取决于你的能源价格，你可能永远收不回这笔投资。但无论你在哪里，它都会减少温室气体排放，希望能源定价也开始反映这一点。哦抱歉，我又讲太深了。

cues.en: What dandelion and companies like it are doing is really important for making geothermal heat pumps more approachable. Simply negating the need to tear up an entire yard is a huge step in the right direction for getting the reluctant on board. But it's by no means a one-size-fits-all solution. Unless you have the right to dig that far down and there's nothing below you that could be a problem like abandoned mines, subway tunnels, etc. Well, you can't do it.
cues.zh: Dandelion 及其同类公司所做的工作，对让地热热泵更易普及非常重要。仅仅是不用把整个院子挖开，就已经是朝正确方向迈出的一大步，能让犹豫的人愿意接受。但这绝不是万能方案。除非你有权挖到那么深，而且下面没有废弃矿井、地铁隧道之类可能出问题的东西。否则，你就做不了。

cues.en: And what about in like, you know, cities? How's a large apartment building going to get all the heat it needs from a borehole? Well it can't. District heating though may be an indirect way to provide geothermally derived heat to large urban spaces. District heating is unfortunately not that common in the US which is a giant shame. Basically it's a network of underground insulated pipes bringing really hot water into buildings that is then fed through radiators to heat them.
cues.zh: 那在城市里呢？一栋大型公寓楼怎么可能靠一个钻孔获得它需要的全部热量？嗯，它做不到。不过，区域供热也许是一种间接方式，把地热产生的热量提供给大型城市空间。不幸的是，区域供热在美国并不太常见，这非常可惜。基本上，它是一套地下保温管道网络，把很热的水送进建筑，再通过散热器供暖。

cues.en: One of the more clever ways to heat that water is with the waste heat of conventional power stations, and many countries have been doing this for decades. It annoys me greatly that this hasn't been normal practice everywhere since power plants have been a thing, especially since water loop systems for heating buildings are by no means a recent development.
cues.zh: 把水加热的一种更聪明的方法，是利用传统发电厂的废热，许多国家几十年来一直都在这么做。自从有了发电厂以来，这种做法居然没有普及到所有地方，这让我非常恼火，尤其是用来给建筑物供暖的水循环系统绝不是什么新鲜事物。

cues.en: But anyway, that practice can be used to provide heat to urban centers without requiring combustion of fuels on-site or the immense electrical supply which would be needed with resistive heating alone. What you use to heat the water then is arbitrary. It could be a large geothermal station running massive heat pumps, or you could even drill deep enough to get heat directly from the magma kilometers below us if you're feeling adventurous.
cues.zh: 但不管怎样，这种做法可以为城市中心提供热量，既不需要在现场燃烧燃料，也不需要单纯依靠电阻加热所带来的庞大供电需求。至于你用什么来加热水，其实很随意。它可以是一个运行大型热泵的巨型地热站，或者如果你想冒险一点，甚至可以直接往地下钻几公里，直接从岩浆中获取热量。

cues.en: This is all stuff that's being researched right now. And as usual, there's pros and cons to every one of these. What gives? Well, Ellen, there are no easy answers. But this video was about heat pumps. While geothermal heat pumps may not exactly work in the concrete jungles of New York City, air source heat pumps certainly can. And maybe they won't make sense to use on really cold days, but really cold days are only some of the days of winter.
cues.zh: 这些都是目前正在研究的内容。而且一如既往，每种方案都有其优缺点。那到底该怎么办呢？好吧，艾伦，这世上没有简单的答案。不过这个视频讲的是热泵。虽然地源热泵可能不太适合纽约这种水泥丛林，但空气源热泵绝对可以。也许在极寒天气里用它们并不划算，但极寒天气在整个冬天里也只是少数几天。

cues.en: We really gotta stop this whole, only solutions which cover every single possible contingency are feasible nonsense and start using what we can when we can. That's kinda my whole point with the every air conditioner should be reversible thing. It's unreasonable to me to limit their potential just because some days heat pumps can't work. We have the technology so use it when possible!
cues.zh: 我们真的不能再抱有那种“只有能应对所有极端情况的方案才可行”的荒谬想法了，而是应该能用就用。这就是我为什么坚持认为“所有空调都应该具备双向制热功能”。在我看来，仅仅因为某些日子热泵无法工作就限制它们的潜力，是完全没有道理的。技术就在这里，能用就用起来啊！

cues.en: Oh yeah, here's a really dumb thing. Electric cars, which nearly universally have air conditioning, are only just now starting to make that reversible. Cabin heat is by far the largest non-locomotive energy use in an EV, and is a large part of why range drops in the winter. It has always been the case that a heat pump would help a lot with that, at least on milder days, and yet even some brand new EV models on sale do not offer them.
cues.zh: 哦对了，还有一件特别蠢的事。电动汽车几乎普遍都配有空调，但直到现在才刚开始让它们具备反向制热功能。车厢供暖是电动车中除行驶外最大的能量消耗，也是冬季续航大打折扣的主要原因。一直以来，热泵都能在这方面提供巨大帮助，至少在天气稍温和时是这样，然而甚至一些在售的全新电动车车型依然没有配备热泵。

cues.en: Instead, resistive heat is your only option. I don't know if there's some trick to ruggedizing reversing valves for road use or maybe there's something else that makes it harder for cars, but come on, heat pumps need to be standard in EVs. Figure it out! And if you can get to a COP of 2 when it's 0 degrees out, fantastic! But you know what's real neat? We're beginning to put heat pumps in more places to do more things besides just heat and cool our living spaces.
cues.zh: 相反，电阻加热是你唯一的选择。我不知道是不是有什么诀窍能让换向阀更耐受道路颠簸，或者汽车上有什么其他难点，但拜托，热泵应该成为电动车的标配。赶紧想办法解决吧！如果你能在摄氏零度时达到 2 的性能系数（COP），那就太棒了！但你知道真正酷的是什么吗？除了给居住空间供暖和制冷之外，我们开始把热泵应用到更多地方去做更多的事情了。

cues.en: Fundamentally, heat pumps are just heat energy relocators and concentrators. If there's a place where we need a lot of heat, we can sometimes take it from another and often with side benefits as well. One real-world application of heat pumps not for heating is the hybrid water heater. Okay, well I suppose that is still heating, but consider a typical North American water heater with a 50 gallon tank. Until recently, you had two choices, electric or gas.
cues.zh: 本质上，热泵只是热能的搬运器和集中器。如果某个地方需要大量热量，我们有时可以从别处取来，还常常附带额外好处。热泵有一个并非用于供暖的实际应用，就是混合式热水器。好吧，我承认这仍然是在加热，但想想典型的北美 50 加仑水箱热水器。直到最近，你只有两个选择：电或燃气。

cues.en: Gas is cheaper to operate but requires venting and also gas. Electric is more expensive to operate, but the device itself is little more than an oversized kettle. Now, the benefit of storing hot water in an insulated tank like this is that you've created a thermal battery. Hybrid water heaters use a heat pump to maintain the water temperature in the tank, or you could say, to keep the battery charged. And it's ultimately getting that energy from the air of the room it's sitting in.
cues.zh: 燃气运行更便宜，但需要排气，也得有燃气。电运行更贵，但设备本身不过是个超大号水壶。把热水储存在这种保温水箱里的好处是，你造出了一个储热电池。混合式热水器用热泵来维持水箱里的水温，或者可以说，让这块电池保持充电。而它最终是从所在房间的空气中获取能量。

cues.en: This not only uses a fraction of the energy that heating the water with electric heating elements does, but provides the additional benefit of free air conditioning and dehumidification in the area around the water heater. To collect the energy it moves into the water, it has an evaporator just like any air conditioner, and it gets cold and wet.
cues.zh: 这不仅只用了电加热元件烧水所耗能量的一小部分，还带来额外好处：热水器周围区域免费获得制冷和除湿效果。为了收集被搬进水里那部分能量，它像任何空调一样有蒸发器，会变冷变湿。

cues.en: This means hybrid water heaters need a drain line to deal with that condensate, but I'd sure like a dehumidifier in my basement that effectively costs less than nothing to run. It's heating my water and more cheaply than before. Of course in the winter this is perhaps a bummer, but if you have gas heat like I do, well now your water heater runs on gas. Just indirectly. And if you had a geothermal heat pump,
cues.zh: 这意味着混合式热水器需要排水管来处理冷凝水，但我真希望地下室里有台除湿机，运行起来实际上等于不花钱还倒赚。它在加热我的水，而且比过去更便宜。当然冬天可能有点扫兴，但如果你像我一样用燃气供暖，那现在你的热水器就靠燃气运行。只是间接靠燃气。而如果你有地源热泵，

cues.en: Well, it would get its heat from the ground after your main heat pump first brought it to your home for you. Anyway, it's a hybrid water heater because these also have traditional heating elements to deal with periods of high demand. The heat pump is slower than good old fashioned hot sticks, but assuming you don't have a shower-thon going on in your house, it can take its time reheating the water in the tank between uses using as little as a quarter the energy of an ordinary electric heater.
cues.zh: 那它就会从地下取热，前提是你的主热泵先把热量带到你家。总之，它叫混合式热水器，是因为这些设备也有传统加热元件来应对高峰需求。热泵比老式加热棒慢，但假设你家没有连着洗个没完的淋浴马拉松，它就能在两次使用之间慢慢重新加热水箱里的水，耗电量最低只有普通电热水器的四分之一。

cues.en: The potential for heat pumps to be used in water heaters, by the way, has made me fairly anti-tankless water heater. It's a myth that tankless water heaters provide you with instant hot water. It still has to get through your pipes. And if you want instant hot water, what you really need is a hot water recirculation system and your plumbing to be completely redone. Or maybe you can get away with point of use booster heaters. But anyway, now that I know that heat pump water heaters are a thing,
cues.zh: 顺便说，热泵用于热水器的潜力，让我相当反对无水箱热水器。无水箱热水器能提供即开即热的热水，这是个误解。热水还是得流过你的管道。如果你想要即开即热的热水，真正需要的是热水循环系统，而且管道得彻底重做。或者也许用使用点辅助加热器就能凑合。但不管怎样，既然我知道热泵热水器确实存在，

cues.en: I have no desire to go tankless. Save that energy, baby! Another really neat development, and perhaps even more so, is the heat pump clothes dryer. Tumble dryers are a sort of guilty pleasure to me. Oh sure, they save tons of time and space, but they also use a lot of energy and are typically vented outside, which not only means there needs to be a vent in the first place, but also creates significant negative pressure when they run. But what do dryers really do?
cues.zh: 我完全不想换成无水箱式。省下那份能量吧，宝贝！另一个非常棒的发展，也许更棒，是热泵干衣机。滚筒烘干机对我来说算是一种带负罪感的享受。哦当然，它们省下大量时间和空间，但也很耗能，而且通常向室外排气，这不仅意味着首先得有个排气口，运行时还会产生明显负压。但烘干机到底在做什么？

cues.en: Well, they basically just tumble clothes around a drum with hot air blowing through it, which makes the clothes dry faster. Making the air hot is the energy intensive part. Buuuuut? That's right! Heat pump it! Heat pump clothes dryers are frankly amazing because it's about the perfect application for the technology. You just need to get the inside of the dryer hotter than the outside.
cues.zh: 烘干机基本上就是让衣服在滚筒里翻滚，同时吹入热风，从而加快烘干速度。而加热空气才是最耗能的环节。但是——？没错！用热泵啊！坦白讲，热泵烘干机简直神了，因为这可以说是该技术的绝配应用。你只需要让烘干机内部的温度比外面更高就行了。

cues.en: Yeah, you could do that with heater coils or even a little gas furnace, but there's plenty of energy from the room it's sitting in for a heat pump to take and concentrate. And none of it gets lost, it just gets concentrated inside. Best of all, you can then exhaust the hot, damp air that exits the drum over the cold evaporator and not only recollect that energy to be pumped back in, but also the moisture from the clothes.
cues.zh: 没错，用电热丝甚至是小型燃气炉也能做到，但它所在的房间里就有大把的能量，完全够热泵提取并汇聚起来。而且这部分能量一点都不会浪费，只会集中到机器内部。最棒的是，你还可以把滚筒排出的湿热空气引流经过冰冷的蒸发器，不仅能回收能量重新泵回内部，还能顺带析出衣服里的水分。

cues.en: You end up with a clothes dryer that needs much less energy to run, doesn't need venting, and can be placed anywhere. Some of them can even be plugged into a standard 120 volt electrical outlet.
cues.zh: 最终你得到的就是一台耗电少得多、无需排气管道、且随处可放的烘干机。有些型号甚至直接插在标准的 120 伏插座上就能用。

cues.en: Heat pump clothes dryers are slower than traditional vented solutions, but they offer great flexibility and a much lower energy cost. Even if you have a gas dryer, eliminating the need for a vent will lower your heating and cooling demand when it runs, thanks to there no longer being a machine blowing the air you paid to heater cool outside. It's really kind of a no-brainer to me. Using a heat pump not only makes it cheaper to run, but solves real problems.
cues.zh: 热泵烘干机虽然比传统的排气式要慢一些，但它灵活性极高，能耗成本也低得多。即使你用的是燃气烘干机，省掉排气管也能在运行时减少室内的冷暖负荷，毕竟再也没有机器把你花钱加热或制冷的空气往室外吹了。在我看来，这真是不二之选。使用热泵不仅运行成本更低，还切实解决了实际问题。

cues.en: That is, if you're willing to have your laundry take longer, which I recognize is not feasible for everyone. Now there is one real downside to the proliferation of heat pumps. To make them, we need refrigerants, and refrigerants have created a whack-a-mole of engineering challenges. When we first ventured down the path of refrigeration, we were using gaseous ammonia as a refrigerant. It was actually a fantastic refrigerant, but it was very toxic and leaks were very dangerous to human life.
cues.zh: 前提是你愿意接受洗烘时间变长，我也承认这点并不是人人都能接受的。不过热泵的大规模普及确实有一个真正的弊端。制造热泵需要制冷剂，而制冷剂带来了一连串按倒葫芦又起瓢的工程挑战。我们最初涉足制冷领域时，使用的是气态氨作为制冷剂。作为制冷剂它其实表现绝佳，但剧毒无比，一旦泄漏对人体生命极其危险。

cues.en: That was the problem that Thomas Midgeley Jr. solved with the creation of Freon. Freon was the first non-toxic, non-flammable refrigerant, and we were thrilled to have it! Of course, decades later we realized the ozone layer was disappearing and we figured out that CFCs like Freon were the culprit. So replacement refrigerants were developed like our friend R134A. These HFCs don't harm the ozone layer, but they are ridiculously potent greenhouse gases.
cues.zh: 这正是 Thomas Midgley Jr. 发明氟利昂所解决的问题。氟利昂是第一种无毒、不易燃的制冷剂，当时能拥有它我们简直欣喜若狂！当然，几十年后我们意识到臭氧层正在消失，并且查明了像氟利昂这样的 CFC 就是罪魁祸首。于是人们又研发出了替代制冷剂，比如我们的老朋友 R134a。这类 HFC 不会破坏臭氧层，但它们却是不折不扣的极强温室气体。

cues.en: This here is over 1,400 times better at trapping heat in the atmosphere than carbon dioxide. Great! Even though in an ideal world it will never leave a refrigerant loop, eventually refrigeration systems develop leaks. If you ever bought one of these to recharge your AC, that's why. So HFCs are being phased out for newer refrigerants like 2,3,3,3 tetrafluoropropene, also known as R-
cues.zh: 就拿这个来说，它在大气中锁住热量的能力是二氧化碳的 1400 多倍。真是“太棒”了！尽管在理想情况下它永远不会漏出制冷循环回路，但制冷系统终究是会出现泄漏的。如果你买过这玩意儿来给空调加氟，原因就在于此。因此 HFC 也正在被淘汰，取而代之的是更新型的制冷剂，比如 2,3,3,3-四氟丙烯，也就是 R-

cues.en: 1, 2, 3, 4, YF. This refrigerant has a global warming potential of less than one, so as far as we can tell, it's harmless. Currently, these new refrigerants are rather expensive, and the reason is patently obvious. It's patents. These next-gen refrigerants are protected by patents and their owners are absolutely okay with exploiting that and hard.
